source.recovery_basis: GitHub Actions job log. The historical CTO generated six CREATE v1 charters and both its local validator and repository validator reported all six valid before the persistence step failed on an untracked-file checkout collision, so dispatch was skipped.
source.body_reconstruction_rule: The six team_ids, priorities, broad domains and portfolio intent are recovered from the historical log/ledger. The failed runner did not persist the 85KB generated JSON and published no artifact, so the detailed charter bodies below are conservative one-cycle reconstructions constrained to those logged scopes. They are HUMAN-FORCED one-shot test charters, not retroactive claims that the wording below is byte-identical to the lost JSON.

batch_rules: Exactly one fresh TEAM attempt per charter.
Independent audit always follows a successful TEAM attempt.
PASS may be integrated once by Frontier Director; REVISE or BLOCKED stops with evidence preserved.
No automatic same-cycle repair, continuation, successor, promotion, or threshold change.
WP-006 remains FALSIFIED at its frozen accepted floors and may not be rerun, rescued, rethresholded, re-represented, or reinterpreted by any charter.
Existing accepted web-physics-volatility-freshness is not duplicated and is not part of this historical batch.
Negative, null, measurement-invalid and data-insufficient outcomes are valid outcomes and must be preserved.

charters.domain: Physics - measurement identifiability and dynamical hypothesis testing in a controlled Web environment
charters.mission: Run one bounded positive-control/negative-control experiment in a controlled Web environment to determine whether a SPIDER-class dynamics instrument can distinguish a deliberately present dynamical structure from a matched structure-absent control without using WP-006's proposition, dataset, thresholds or rescue logic.
charters.question: Can a preregistered Web-dynamics measurement pipeline recover a known injected dynamical effect in a controlled environment while remaining null on a matched live-arm negative control?
charters.why_now: Historical CTO #25 ranked this CRITICAL as the cleanest way to separate future instrument sensitivity from future domain hypotheses after WP-006 closed. A one-shot calibration result can bound what later Physics programs are capable of measuring without changing any historical verdict.
charters.why_not_existing_lane: The core Physics lane is DORMANT and WP-006 is closed. This is a new controlled identifiability question, not a continuation of WP-006.
charters.expected_work_compression_leverage: A validated calibration harness prevents future teams from spending full cycles on instruments that cannot detect known-present structure; a failed calibration is equally useful because it blocks unsupported future physics claims early.
evidence_inputs: Historical CTO #25 run 32909350978: exact team id, CREATE v1, CRITICAL, domain beginning 'Physics - measurement identifiability and dynamical hypothesis testing'.
Accepted Physics state: WP-006 FALSIFIED and core lane DORMANT; V3 permits orthogonal Physics programs while forbidding rescue.
Historical CTO #25 ledger summary: controlled-web-lab required a named primary question and matched live-arm negative control.
charters.strongest_null_or_baseline: Matched structure-absent control generated with the same environment, sampling budget, preprocessing, scoring code and evaluation schedule; plus a trivial persistence/constant predictor where applicable. The injected-effect arm and null arm must be indistinguishable to the evaluator except for the preregistered intervention.
validity_threats: Detector reads injector metadata or fixture labels instead of dynamics.
Positive-control effect is so large or synthetic that the test says nothing about measurement sensitivity near realistic effect sizes.
Control and treatment differ in nuisance variables such as timing, page identity or action count.
Any attempt to use the result to reinterpret WP-006 is forbidden.
required_artifacts: Frozen preregistration before outcome inspection.
Controlled fixture/injector specification and independent detector path.
Raw treatment/null rows with provenance and deterministic recomputation script.
Single one-shot verdict with explicit claim ceiling and WP-006 non-rescue statement.
charters.stop_condition: Stop after this one audited attempt regardless of PASS/REVISE/BLOCKED or scientific direction. No automatic repair or continuation. A failed measurement is recorded MEASUREMENT_INVALID rather than tuned until positive.

charters.domain: Physics - temporal volatility and characteristic-time structure of Web knowledge
charters.mission: Run one bounded test of whether already available or cheaply collectible Web-state observations show predictive temporal volatility structure beyond simple recency/site/page-class priors, without duplicating the accepted web-physics-volatility-freshness team's lifecycle or claiming a general Web timescale.
charters.question: Does a preregistered volatility representation improve held-out change prediction beyond recency, site identity, page class and constant-hazard baselines under leave-one-site-out evaluation?
charters.why_now: Historical CTO #25 ranked this CRITICAL and explicitly demanded recency/site/page-class nulls with leave-one-site-out testing. One cycle can test whether the apparent freshness idea contains information beyond obvious metadata.
charters.why_not_existing_lane: The current accepted volatility team tests its own chartered staged program. This historical one-shot is a separate bounded falsification using the CTO #25 comparison discipline and cannot auto-continue or supersede that team.
charters.expected_work_compression_leverage: If volatility beyond trivial priors is absent, SPIDER should avoid elaborate freshness models; if it survives, it identifies which metadata-free residual is worth carrying into capsule invalidation work.
evidence_inputs: Historical CTO #25 run 32909350978: exact team id, CREATE v1, CRITICAL, domain beginning 'Physics - temporal volatility and characteristic-time structure of Web'.
Historical CTO #25 ledger summary: recency/site/page-class null battery and leave-one-site-out hardening were binding.
Accepted current Frontier evidence may be read as prior evidence but must not be silently pooled into the confirmatory one-shot.
charters.strongest_null_or_baseline: Recency-only, site-identity, page-class, site×page-class constant-hazard and shuffled-time baselines; primary generalization test is leave-one-site-out or the strongest feasible site holdout supported by the available data.
validity_threats: Duplicating or double-counting the existing volatility/freshness team's evidence.
Calendar or site identity masquerading as temporal mechanics.
Sparse change events making characteristic times unidentifiable.
Post-hoc choice of aggregation window or volatility metric.
required_artifacts: One-shot preregistration with frozen representation, null battery and holdout rule.
Data provenance map identifying any overlap with existing Frontier evidence.
Held-out comparison table including all trivial priors.
Single verdict with overlap and data-adequacy ceiling.
charters.stop_condition: One audited attempt only. Stop with FALSIFIED, SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST, DATA_INSUFFICIENT or MEASUREMENT_INVALID as appropriate; no automatic repair/continuation.

charters.domain: Physics - uncertainty and reliability structure for exploration-budget allocation
charters.mission: Use existing accepted datasets and run records in one bounded reanalysis to test whether observable uncertainty/reliability features predict where additional exploration budget is actually useful, rather than treating all novel states/actions equally.
charters.question: Can pre-action uncertainty or local reliability features predict marginal value of additional exploration budget better than fixed-budget, random-allocation and simple novelty-count baselines on held-out tasks/sites?
charters.why_now: Historical CTO #25 selected Physics family #7 specifically because reanalysis of existing data was the cheapest strong test. It can produce a bounded yes/no result without new live collection.
charters.why_not_existing_lane: Graph optimizes addressing and Runtime executes capsules; neither owns a falsifiable study of the mapping from uncertainty structure to marginal exploration value.
charters.expected_work_compression_leverage: A useful budget-allocation signal directly reduces repeated browser/reasoning spend by concentrating novelty cost where expected information gain is highest; a null result rules out a speculative scheduler layer.
evidence_inputs: Historical CTO #25 run 32909350978: exact team id, CREATE v1, HIGH, Physics exploration-budget domain.
Historical CTO #25 ledger summary: Physics family #7 reanalysis on existing datasets was the cheapest strong test.
Accepted Graph/Physics/Runtime result tables may be used only with their existing evidence ceilings and provenance.
charters.strongest_null_or_baseline: Fixed equal budget, random budget permutation, novelty-count-only allocation and the strongest cheap heuristic already derivable from the same pre-action information. Evaluation must be task/site held out where data permit.
validity_threats: Outcome leakage: budget predictor uses post-action success or future trajectory information.
Selection bias from only observing budgets actually chosen by prior policies.
Different environments/tasks confound uncertainty with inherent difficulty.
Retrospective metric shopping across existing logs.
required_artifacts: Frozen reanalysis protocol naming eligible historical rows before scoring.
Feature availability audit proving all predictor inputs are pre-action.
Null/baseline comparison with held-out grouping and uncertainty intervals.
One-shot verdict and explicit causal/non-causal ceiling.
charters.stop_condition: Stop after the single preregistered historical reanalysis and audit. No new collection, automatic repair, or continuation in this batch.

charters.domain: Agent decision economics - inheritance-boundary prediction and verification economics
charters.mission: Run one bounded experiment testing whether SPIDER can cheaply decide when inherited work should be trusted/reused versus when novel exploration is economically preferable, including retrieval/applicability/verification overhead in the decision.
charters.question: Does an evidence-only novelty/reuse gate reduce total repeat cost at matched success versus always-reuse and always-explore policies after charging retrieval, applicability, verification and recovery costs?
charters.why_now: Historical CTO #25 created this HIGH-priority team and explicitly folded verification economics into it. It attacks the central SPIDER decision boundary rather than another raw success benchmark.
charters.why_not_existing_lane: Runtime exposes applicability/verification events and Product measures economics, but no lane owns the cross-cutting gate that predicts whether reuse itself is worth attempting.
charters.expected_work_compression_leverage: This is directly aligned with SPIDER's north star: pay novelty cost only when needed. A negative result is valuable if simple always-explore or always-reuse dominates after full overhead accounting.
evidence_inputs: Historical CTO #25 run 32909350978: exact team id, CREATE v1, HIGH, agent-decision-economics domain.
Historical CTO #25 ledger summary: novelty-gating absorbs verification economics.
Accepted Runtime and Graph evidence must retain their claim ceilings; no zero-provider pilot may be relabeled as real-LLM economics.
charters.strongest_null_or_baseline: Always explore/cold policy, always attempt best available inherited candidate, and a simple deterministic applicability-only gate. Charge all retrieval, applicability, verification, fallback and recovery overhead symmetrically.
validity_threats: Gate trains or tunes on the same tasks used for evaluation.
Verification cost omitted or charged asymmetrically.
Gate has access to outcome labels unavailable at decision time.
Success differences rather than cost differences drive apparent savings.
required_artifacts: Frozen decision-time feature set and cost accounting contract.
Matched-success comparison against all three baselines.
Per-task decomposition of retrieval/applicability/verification/recovery/novelty cost.
One-shot verdict including break-even conditions where estimable.
charters.stop_condition: Stop after one audited experiment. REVISE preserves required fixes but triggers no repair; PASS integrates once with auto_continue_allowed=false.

charters.domain: Operational-memory maintenance - scoped delta-learning and minimal repair after drift
charters.mission: Run one controlled mutation experiment testing whether a previously valid capability can be repaired by changing only the genuinely invalid segment, with scoped negative knowledge, more cheaply than full relearning while preserving unaffected behavior.
charters.question: Under preregistered disjoint mutations, can scoped delta repair restore success with fewer novel actions/edits than full relearning and without corrupting unaffected capability segments?
charters.why_now: Historical CTO #25 created this HIGH-priority team. The Capability Capsule contract promises delta learning, but accepted evidence for localized repair remains thin; a synthetic/controlled one-shot can test the mechanism without waiting for production drift.
charters.why_not_existing_lane: Runtime currently refuses unsupported maintenance machinery and Graph stores evidence; neither owns a standalone controlled falsification of minimal repair locality.
charters.expected_work_compression_leverage: If repair locality holds, future agents pay only for changed segments. If it fails, SPIDER avoids building a fragile patch subsystem and can prefer full invalidation/re-exploration.
evidence_inputs: Historical CTO #25 run 32909350978: exact team id, CREATE v1, HIGH.
Historical CTO #25 ledger: scoped-delta-repair was one of the six independent Frontier openings.
Capability Capsule delta-learning principle is a hypothesis to test, not accepted evidence.
charters.strongest_null_or_baseline: Full relearning from scratch under identical mutation and budget, plus no-repair replay as a failure sanity check. Use disjoint mutations so untouched segments provide corruption controls.
validity_threats: Mutation labels directly reveal the repair location.
Repair benchmark is too local/trivial relative to full relearning baseline.
Unaffected segments are not reverified, hiding collateral corruption.
Scoped negative knowledge is credited without measuring its retrieval/update cost.
required_artifacts: Frozen mutation family and hidden mutation assignment.
Base capability provenance and pre-mutation verification.
Repair-vs-full-relearn cost and success rows including unaffected-segment checks.
Scoped negative-knowledge artifact plus one-shot verdict.
charters.stop_condition: Exactly one audited mutation/repair cycle. No automatic repair of the research cycle and no second mutation family in this batch.

charters.domain: Cross-lane measurement methodology - evaluation-fixture comparability, instrument provenance and spentness
charters.mission: Build and exercise once a minimal machine-readable instrument ledger on existing accepted Graph/Physics/Intel/Runtime evidence to determine whether evaluation fixtures, adaptation history and instrument spentness can be tracked well enough to prevent cross-lane instrument reuse and hidden selection-on-instrument.
charters.question: Can a minimal provenance/spentness ledger mechanically flag known instrument-reuse, post-adaptation and comparability hazards in accepted SPIDER evidence without inventing scientific verdicts?
charters.why_now: Historical CTO #25 created this HIGH-priority cross-lane team after repeated instrument-spending and report/data-drift incidents. It is cheap because it can operate on existing provenance.
charters.why_not_existing_lane: Each lane tracks its own experiments but no lane owns cross-lane evaluation-fixture identity, authorship/adaptation history and spentness semantics.
charters.expected_work_compression_leverage: A useful ledger prevents expensive invalid confirmatory cycles and duplicated forensic archaeology; if it cannot reliably classify existing cases, it should not become orchestration infrastructure.
evidence_inputs: Historical CTO #25 run 32909350978: exact team id, CREATE v1, HIGH, cross-lane measurement-methodology domain.
Historical CTO #25 ledger: instrument-ledger partially owns the instrument-spending cascade.
Run Evidence Memory may be used as radar with evidence_status preserved; it may not upgrade scientific claims.
charters.strongest_null_or_baseline: Current per-lane provenance fields/manual ledger review. The new ledger must catch a preregistered set of already-known provenance/spentness hazards with no false scientific reclassification and with lower lookup ambiguity than manual status quo.
validity_threats: Encoding the known answers manually rather than deriving them from durable provenance.
Treating missing provenance as clean provenance instead of UNKNOWN.
Changing or summarizing away original evidence status/verdicts.
Creating more orchestration burden than the forensic work it removes.
required_artifacts: Minimal ledger schema with UNKNOWN-safe semantics.
One-time backfill of a preregistered sample across at least three lanes.
Mechanical hazard checks and comparison against manual baseline.
One-shot verdict on whether the ledger is worth retaining; no automatic deployment.
charters.stop_condition: Stop after one backfill/check/audit cycle. The batch does not authorize making the ledger mandatory infrastructure or auto-continuing the team.
